Yes—you should be able to spot it quite easily.

The Moon is high in the southwest: altitude **37.4°**, azimuth **217.3°** (southwest, measured clockwise from north). At **25.9% illumination**, it is a fairly conspicuous crescent, and with the Sun **13.5° below the horizon**, the sky is already in astronomical twilight and quite dark. The clear sky and the Moon’s large angular size make unaided visibility very likely.

Look roughly **37° above the southwestern horizon**—about two-fifths of the way from the horizon to the zenith. It should be obvious once you scan that area, though the thin crescent may be less dazzling than a half or full Moon. Its distance is not relevant to practical visibility.
